prompt: Once children start school, teachers have more influence on their intellectual and social development than parents do. To what extent do you agree or disagree? Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
essay:
It is argued that once children start school, teachers have a greater influence than parents on children's intellectual and social development. This essay disagrees with this view because parents continue to guide their children's learning and play the most important role in shaping their social behaviour.

Parents still have a strong influence on their children’s intellectual development after they start school. The first thing is that parents encourage their children to study, help them with homework, and develop good learning habits at home. As a result, children are more likely to achieve better academic results. For example, when the child finds mathematics difficult, parents can spend time explaining lessons, practise exercises together, and encourage the child to keep trying instead of giving up. Therefore, parents continue to play an essential role in their children’s education.

Moreover, parents have a greater impact on children’s social development because they teach values and behaviour through everyday life. Children spend a lot of time with their families, where they learn how to communicate, respect others, and solve problems politely. For instance, when children argue with their brothers or sisters, parents often teach them to apologise, share their belongings, and respect each other’s feelings. These experiences help children develop good manners and build healthy relationships with other people.

In conclusion, although teachers make an important contribution to children’s education and social skills at school, I believe that parents continue to have the greatest influence on both their intellectual and social development.
